observation_summary: The FastDateFormat class caches instances based on a key that does not correctly account for changes in the default Locale. When the default Locale is changed, subsequent calls to getDateInstance() or getDateTimeInstance() return cached instances created with the old default Locale instead of the new one.
hypothesis: The caching mechanism for FastDateFormat instances uses a key that fails to incorporate the current default Locale when no explicit locale is provided. Consequently, the cache returns stale instances that were initialized with a previous default Locale.
prediction: The code responsible for generating the cache key in FastDateFormat will be missing the current default Locale in its construction, or it will be using a static reference to the default Locale that is not updated when the system default changes.
experiment_rationale: The failure occurs because the system expects a new instance (or at least one matching the current default locale) after changing the default locale, but receives a cached instance from the previous state. This indicates the caching logic (the algorithm for retrieving/creating instances) is flawed regarding its dependency on the environment state.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the caching algorithm. The method responsible for retrieving instances uses a key that does not correctly reflect the current system state (the default Locale). This is a procedural error in how the cache key is constructed and how the cache is invalidated or updated, fitting the Algorithm/Method category as it involves the logic of the retrieval procedure.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The FastDateFormat getDateInstance() and getDateTimeInstance() methods create the HashMap key from various items including the locale. If the locale is null, then it is not made part of the key, but the stored object is created using the current default locale. If the Locale is changed subsequently, then the wrong locale is applied.'
The failing tests show that after changing the default locale, the system returns an instance associated with the old locale (en_US) instead of the new one (de_DE).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the initialization of the cache key is involved, the core issue is the procedural logic of the caching algorithm failing to account for dynamic environment changes.
There is no missing guard or validation; the logic is simply using an insufficient key for the cache, which is an algorithmic design choice for the cache retrieval.
